Cage's modified piano with objects between strings.
Style using repeated cells and gradual process, from 1960s.
American minimalist (b. 1937), additive and arpeggiated cells.

walkthroughs.body_html: John Cage's 4'33" premiered on 29 August 1952 at Woodstock, NY. David Tudor sat at the piano playing no notes for four minutes and thirty-three seconds. Ambient sound became the work.
Minimalism emerged in 1960s New York. Steve Reich's It's Gonna Rain (1965) used tape phasing. Philip Glass's Music in Twelve Parts (1971-74) used additive process.
Reich's manifesto 'Music as a Gradual Process' (1968) describes works whose form is identical to the process generating them — the listener follows transformation in real time.
